correctness.rationale: For each rank, support maximization over zero-one indicators gives exactly the upper-minus-lower Gaussian order-statistic sum divided by an independent chi radius. DKW control of the empirical quantiles gives an \(o_{L^2}(\sqrt n)\) symmetric trimmed-sum linearization for any fixed positive rank fraction. Joint Gaussian CLT plus the exact radial expansion produces the covariance kernel. The actual covariance limits follow from the exact independence identity for Gaussian radius and directional widths, rather than weak convergence alone. Gaussian integration verifies the mixed moments and the normalization correction. The derivative of the half-rank covariance has one positive zero by a two-root quadratic derivative analysis, proving a single covariance zero. The packaged reproducible checker verifies finite identities, six mixed Gaussian moments, the bracketed threshold and simulated signs, without using finite data as proof of infinite limits.

value.rationale: Rank-indexed hypersimplices are natural uniform-matroid polytopes in one canonical Euclidean space; jointly measuring their directional widths reveals dependence between two geometric scales of the same direction. The exact kernel isolates a negative dependence induced by unit-sphere normalization, reversing the nonnegative leading covariance of corresponding raw Gaussian trimmed sums. A unique explicitly located rank threshold separates both signs. This is a structural, experimentally testable geometric distinction across an infinite family rather than a cosmetic rewrite of a standard mean-width identity.
